 1   Cuomo to proclaim March 2015 as Women's History 

 2   Month in the State of New York.  

 3                "WHEREAS, March is Women's History 

 4   Month; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, March 8th is International 

 6   Women's Day; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, Each year New York State 

 8   officially sets aside time to recognize the 

 9   unique contributions that women have made to 

10   New York and its society; and 

11                "WHEREAS, New York State has a 

12   distinguished history of monumental achievements 

13   in the area of women's rights; and 

14                "WHEREAS, In 1826, New York State 

15   opened one of the first public high schools for 

16   girls, resulting in a future for women in which 

17   they were no longer confined to the home, a 

18   future in which they were educated and able to 

19   use this education to better their social and  

20   economic status; and 

21                "WHEREAS, In 1848 in New York, the 

22   first women's rights convention was held at 

23   Seneca Falls to secure for all women the right to 

24   vote; and 

25                "WHEREAS, In 1903, The Women's Trade

 1   Union League of New York was formed to represent 

 2   working women, later becoming the nucleus for the 

 3   International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, In 1918, one year after 

 5   New York guaranteed women the right to vote in 

 6   all elections, the first two women, Ida Sammis 

 7   and Mary Lilly, were elected to the New York 

 8   State Legislature; and 

 9                "WHEREAS, In 1967, Muriel Siebert 

10   became the first woman to own a seat on the 

11   New York Stock Exchange, opening the door for 

12   women to gain positions of greater economic 

13   power; and

15   the site of the first Women's Strike for 

16   Equality, in which 50,000 people marched for 

17   equal rights; and

19   Assemblywoman Shirley Chisholm became the first 

20   black woman elected to Congress and in 1972, she 

21   ran for President of the United States, another

24   women legislators established the Legislative  

25   Women's Caucus to improve the participation of

12   come to pay tribute to many of our nation's 

13   talented women who have fought and overcome

16   first Congressional resolution, and since 1987

18   this entire month of March.

20   New York where some of the most impressive 

21   achievements in the area of women's rights has 

22   occurred.  From the opening of the first public 

23   school for girls, the first women's rights 

24   convention, those women who were leading pioneers 

25   in the fields of medicine and law, those who

12   how far we've come, we cannot ignore the

16   domestic violence, discrimination in the
